# Behavioral Specification for ENTROPY_SRC

## 1. Overview

The ENTROPY_SRC module provides the register-visible and hardware-visible interface to an entropy generation subsystem. In normal operation, it collects raw bits from an external physical noise source, subjects them to health testing, conditions them into full-entropy words, and makes those words available to firmware or to a hardware entropy consumer.

The module may also be configured at design time to operate in a deterministic emulation mode. In that mode, it does not consume an external noise source and does not perform real health testing or conditioning; instead, it supplies a firmware-seeded deterministic data stream through the same delivery paths.

All module outputs must be at known, safe states after reset. The module must be disabled by default after reset and must not generate entropy, interrupts, or alerts until enabled.

## 2. Operating Modes

### 2.1 Normal Mode

In normal mode, the module shall:

- Request randomness from the external physical noise source only while enabled.
- Accept raw random samples only when they are presented as valid by the external source.
- Ignore incoming random data when disabled.
- Collect raw bits into internal blocks before performing health tests.
- Perform the required health checks on the raw bit stream.
- Condition approved raw entropy into output entropy words.
- Indicate whether each delivered entropy word is FIPS-compliant.
- Deliver entropy words to the hardware entropy interface and/or to the firmware-visible entropy data path.

### 2.2 Deterministic Emulation Mode

When the module is configured for deterministic emulation mode, the following behavior shall apply:

- The register interface remains active and accessible.
- The module shall not consume data from the external physical noise source.
- The module shall not generate halt requests, external health-test activity, or health-test-related alerts.
- The module shall generate deterministic pseudo-random data from a firmware-programmable seed.
- The seed shall be loaded when the module is enabled and shall advance while the module remains enabled.
- When disabled, the deterministic generator shall not advance.
- If disabled and then re-enabled, the module shall reload the seed.
- The generated deterministic value shall be visible through the firmware entropy data path and through the hardware entropy delivery path.
- The entropy-valid interrupt shall be active while the module is enabled.
- Other interrupts and alerts shall not be generated.

## 3. Register Interface and Access Control

The module shall provide a memory-mapped register interface. Through this interface, firmware shall be able to:

- Enable or disable the entropy source.
- Select operating mode, entropy routing, and boot-time behavior.
- Program health-test thresholds, windows, and enables.
- Read health-test status, counters, and watermark values.
- Read entropy words.
- Configure interrupts and alerts.
- Read status and debug information.

The module shall enforce register locking. Once firmware locks configuration registers, subsequent writes to locked fields shall be ignored.

The module shall expose two one-time-programmable capability inputs. These inputs use a multibit encoding, and the module shall interpret only the strict-true value as enabling the associated capability.

- The firmware-read capability must be true before firmware can read entropy data directly.
- The firmware-override capability must be true before the firmware override data path can be used.

If a capability is not strictly true, the corresponding function shall be unavailable.

The module shall detect integrity violations on the bus interface. If such a violation is detected, the module shall report it as a fatal alert condition.

## 4. Entropy Delivery

### 4.1 Firmware Data Path

The module shall provide a register-visible entropy data register. When a complete entropy word is available, the module shall indicate this through the entropy-valid interrupt and status interface. Firmware shall be able to read the entropy word in 32-bit chunks.

The module must not allow firmware to read entropy words if the firmware-read capability is disabled.

### 4.2 Hardware Entropy Interface

The module shall provide a hardware entropy delivery interface using a request/acknowledge protocol.

- The module shall drive a wide entropy word only when it has valid data to deliver.
- The module shall accompany each delivered word with a FIPS-compliance indicator.
- The module shall assert its acknowledge only when it is presenting valid entropy data.
- A transfer shall occur when the requesting side indicates readiness and the module indicates valid data.
- Each transfer shall consume one stored entropy word.

If the final entropy storage becomes full, newly generated health-tested entropy may be intentionally discarded. This intentional discard shall not corrupt previously stored entropy and shall not, by itself, cause an interrupt or alert.

### 4.3 FIPS Indication

The module shall provide a dedicated output indicating whether the entropy source is currently operating in FIPS-compliant mode. This output shall be asserted only when the full FIPS/CC health-test and conditioning path is active.

Each entropy word delivered on the hardware entropy interface shall also include a FIPS flag. Words delivered after full conditioning shall be marked FIPS-compliant. Words delivered during boot-time mode, from a bypass path, or from a firmware-processed path shall not be marked FIPS-compliant unless the configuration explicitly permits such marking.

## 5. Health Testing

In normal mode, the module shall run the following health tests on the raw noise bit stream:

- Repetition Count Test, which detects long runs of identical bits.
- Adaptive Proportion Test, which detects bias in the number of ones in a window.
- Bucket Test, which detects bias in the distribution of multi-bit symbols.
- Markov Test, which detects unexpected first-order temporal correlation in each bit stream.

Each health test shall have:

- An enable/disable control.
- A configurable threshold or thresholds.
- A configurable window size where applicable.
- Separate configuration for boot-time mode and normal mode where required.

The module shall update health-test status and statistics as tests are performed. This includes counts of failures and observed watermark values.

Health-test counters shall be reset when the module is disabled.

A health-test failure shall increment the relevant failure counters. When health-test failure activity crosses the programmed alert threshold, the module shall:

- Assert the recoverable alert.
- Assert the health-test-failed interrupt.

If the alert threshold is programmed to zero, alert generation from health-test failures shall be disabled.

## 6. Conditioning and Boot-Time Operation

In normal full-compliance operation, the module shall accumulate a block of raw bits that have passed health testing, pass them through a conditioning function, and produce a smaller full-entropy output word.

The module shall support a boot-time mode. In boot-time mode:

- A reduced health-test window is used, allowing an initial seed to be produced with lower latency.
- The initial seed may be delivered without the normal full conditioning path.
- Entropy delivered in boot-time mode shall be marked as non-FIPS.

Once boot-time operation completes, the module shall switch to normal FIPS-compliant operation unless configured otherwise.

## 7. Firmware Override and Observation Path

The module shall support a firmware override data path when the corresponding capability is enabled. In this mode:

- Raw entropy may be routed to a firmware-accessible buffer instead of, or in addition to, the normal health-test and conditioning path.
- Firmware may read raw entropy, process it, and write processed entropy back.
- The module shall accept returned data and insert it into the entropy stream.
- The module shall not use the firmware override path unless the firmware-override capability is true and the feature is enabled by configuration.

The module shall also provide an observation FIFO status/interrupt path. The observe-FIFO-ready interrupt shall indicate when the observation FIFO is ready for a transfer, as defined by the register specification.

## 8. External Health-Test Interface

The module shall provide an external health-test interface for vendor-specific health checks.

In normal mode, the module shall:

- Present raw entropy symbols to the external health-test logic.
- Indicate when each raw entropy symbol is valid.
- Drive configuration outputs for test window, high threshold, low threshold, active, and clear as programmed by firmware.
- Accept external health-test failure indications and test-count results.
- Incorporate external health-test failures into the same health-test reporting and alert mechanism used for internal tests.

In deterministic emulation mode, the external health-test interface shall be held inactive.

## 9. Interrupts

The module shall provide the following interrupts:

- **Entropy-valid interrupt**: asserted when entropy data is available for firmware to read.
- **Health-test-failed interrupt**: asserted when a health-test failure crosses the programmed alert threshold.
- **Observe-FIFO-ready interrupt**: asserted when the observation FIFO becomes ready for transfer.
- **Fatal-error interrupt**: asserted when an internal fatal error condition is detected, such as an illegal internal FIFO operation or an integrity check failure.

Interrupts shall be maskable and clearable through the register interface.

## 10. Alerts

The module shall provide two alert channels:

- A recoverable alert channel, used for health-test failure conditions.
- A fatal alert channel, used for fatal internal error conditions and bus integrity violations.

The module shall also allow software to trigger an alert-test operation through registers. Alert-test operations shall exercise the alert output path without requiring an actual alert condition.

The fatal alert shall be asserted when an internal fatal error condition is detected or when a bus integrity violation is detected on the register interface.

In deterministic emulation mode, alert channels shall remain inactive.

## 11. Coordination Halt Interface

The module shall include a coordination halt interface used to protect entropy transfers that must not be interrupted by certain downstream operations.

- The module shall assert the halt request when it needs the cooperating block to be halted for an entropy-related operation.
- The module shall wait for the halt acknowledgment before completing the protected operation if required.
- The module shall deassert the halt request when the protected operation completes, when the module is disabled, or in deterministic emulation mode.

## 12. Disable and Shutdown Behavior

When firmware clears the enable control in normal mode, the module shall:

- Stop requesting new randomness from the external noise source.
- Stop accepting new raw samples.
- Reset health-test counters and state.
- Cease delivering new entropy words.
- Finish any handshakes already in progress in an orderly way.
- Report through status when the internal state machine has reached idle.

Once idle status is reported, firmware may safely re-enable the module.

# entropy_src_bucket_ht Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the bucket health test for the entropy source. It observes a stream of entropy symbols, maintains a separate count for each possible symbol value, and, at the end of each test window, checks whether any symbol count exceeds a programmable threshold.

The module is intended to detect an unexpectedly frequent symbol value in a window of entropy data.

## 2. External Behavior

### 2.1 Clock and Reset

- The module is a synchronous design.
- On reset, all bucket counts shall be cleared to zero.
- After reset, the failure indication shall be inactive, the counter-error indication shall be inactive, and the diagnostic maximum count shall be zero.

### 2.2 Symbol Counting

- The module accepts entropy symbols. For the default 4-bit symbol width, there are 16 possible symbol values, and the module maintains 16 corresponding buckets.
- When a valid symbol is presented while counting is enabled, the module shall increment the bucket whose index equals the numeric value of that symbol.
- Exactly one bucket shall be incremented per valid symbol.
- Symbol value 0 shall increment the first bucket; symbol value 15 shall increment the last bucket.
- Symbols presented while counting is disabled or while the clear control is asserted shall be ignored.

### 2.3 Enable and Clear Behavior

- The test has an active enable control.
- When the enable control is deasserted, all bucket counters shall be held at zero, and no incoming symbols shall be counted.
- When the clear control is asserted, all bucket counters shall be cleared to zero.
- The clear control shall take precedence over any simultaneous valid-symbol increment.
- Deasserting enable or asserting clear shall discard any partial-window counts. Counting, once re-enabled or un-cleared, shall start again from zero.

### 2.4 Window Boundary Evaluation

- A window-boundary pulse marks the end of the current fixed-size test window.
- When a window-boundary pulse is asserted while the test is enabled, the module shall compare every bucket count against the threshold.
- If any bucket count is strictly greater than the threshold, the failure output shall be asserted.
- A bucket count exactly equal to the threshold shall not cause a failure.
- After the comparison, all bucket counters shall be cleared for the next window.
- If the window-boundary pulse is asserted while the test is disabled, no failure output shall be generated, and the counters shall remain cleared.
- Each window is independent: counts shall not accumulate across windows.

### 2.5 Threshold Comparison

- The threshold is an unsigned value.
- The comparison uses the threshold value present at the time the window-boundary pulse is evaluated.
- A threshold of zero means that any non-zero bucket count in a window causes a failure.
- A threshold larger than any count in the window shall not cause a failure.

## 3. Outputs

### 3.1 Failure Indication

- The failure output shall be asserted only at a window boundary and only when the test is enabled and at least one bucket count exceeds the threshold.
- The failure indication is not sticky. It reflects the result of the most recent window evaluation.
- It indicates a statistical bucket-test failure, not a hardware counter error.

### 3.2 Diagnostic Maximum Count

- The module shall provide a diagnostic output equal to the largest count currently present in any bucket.
- This is a maximum-value output, not the sum of all bucket counts.
- When all counters are zero, the diagnostic maximum count shall be zero.
- This output provides visibility into how close the busiest bucket is to the threshold.

### 3.3 Counter-Integrity Error

- The module shall assert a counter-error output whenever any bucket counter detects an internal counting inconsistency.
- This output is separate from the bucket-test failure output.
- It shall be asserted if any one or more bucket counters report such an error.
- This output indicates a potential hardware reliability problem, not a statistical property of the entropy data.

## 4. Initialization and Control Conditions

- After reset, counting does not begin until the test is enabled and the clear control is deasserted.
- When the module is enabled, clear is deasserted, and valid symbols are presented, counting shall begin immediately from zero.
- If the enable control is later deasserted, all accumulated counts shall be discarded.
- If the clear control is later asserted, all accumulated counts shall be discarded.
- A valid symbol presented on the same cycle as a window-boundary pulse shall not be counted; the boundary clearing behavior takes precedence.

## 5. Summary of Functional Requirements

- Classify each valid entropy symbol into its corresponding bucket.
- Count symbols within the current window only.
- Reset counts at each window boundary.
- Report a failure when any bucket count exceeds the threshold at the window boundary.
- Report the current maximum bucket count as a diagnostic value.
- Report any detected counter-integrity error separately from the statistical failure result.
- Ensure that disabling the test or asserting clear produces clean, zeroed state.
